It also contained unpermitted synthetic colour.
There is violation of Rue 32(e) and (f) PFA Rules".

I have considered the submissions and have gone through the judgements.
28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) 21
Before I take the judgements cited by the parties, I would like to mention that a judgement can't be applied in a mechanical manner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kesar Devi Vs. Union of India 2003 VII AD (SC) 468 has held as under: " The judgment of a court is not to be interpreted like a statute where every word, as far as possible, has to be given a literal meaning and no word is to be ignored.

entities.text: Kesar Devi Vs. Union of India 2003 VII AD (SC) 468
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The observations made have to be understood in the context of facts and contentions raised."

22 The arguments of ld. Counsel for the Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
3 appellant are two fold.

sentences.text: 23 In the first instance it is the argument that in view of the law referred to above, the appellant is entitled to acquittal solely on the ground that the reports of the Public Analyst and the Director CFL were at variance exceeding .3 %.
24 Secondly the receipt produced by Deepak Kalra was forged and the mustard oil in question had not been sold by the appellant to him.
25 First of all I shall take judgements.

26 Since Kashi Nath's judgement (supra) is based on Bishan Sarup's judgement (supra) rendered by the Full Bench of the Hon'ble 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court, decided on 19/9/2005 therefore, let me mention the facts of these two cases and the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court in these cases.

entities.text: 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27 In Bishan Sarup 's case (supra) a sample of cow's milk was taken on 27/3/1962.
On analysis by the Public Analyst vide his report dated 31/3/1962 the fat contents were found to be 6.7% and the non fatty solids were found to be 8.03% as against the prescribed standard of 8.5%.
Since the non fatty solids were found to be deficient, therefore, the milk was declared to be adulterated.
I need not touch the defence of the respondents (accused) in that case.
During trial, after a lapse of about a year and 10 months Bishan Sarup had prayed on 27/8/1964 that the sample of the milk in possession of the MCD be sent to the Director, CFL.
Initially the application was rejected by the Ld. Magistrate.
However, the order was reviewed on 4/5/1965 and the sample was sent to the Director, CFL.
On 23/4/1965 the Director had sent his report wherein he had mentioned that the fat contents of the milk were 7.2% and the non fatty solids were 6.4%.
The Director, CFL also declared the sample to be adulterated.

The Ld. MM took the view that "there was something infringing about 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) the report of Director, CFL because it was surprising that the Director, CFL was able to analyze the sample even after such great lapse of time".
28

The Ld. MM gave benefit of doubt and acquitted both the respondents (accused).
29
The MCD preferred the appeal.

30 Since the question of right of the accused to have the second sample examined under section 13 (2) of the Act and the effect of the time lapse during the process was involved, therefore, Full Bench of the Hon'ble High Court had been constituted.
31 The Hon'ble High Court took into account the earlier decisions.
32 In para 10 and 17A it was observed as under: "10

The consideration of the time lapse between the date of the taking of the sample, the launching of the prosecution and the date when the sample was sent to the Director of Central Food Laboratory is relevant only for this purpose.

Once the Director of Central Food Laboratory has examined the 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA)
sample and has delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is the final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein.

The presumption attaching to the certificate again is only in regard to what is stated in it as to the contents of the sample Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
4 actually examined by the Director and nothing more.

entities.text: Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even after this certificate, it is open to the accused to show that in the facts of a given case and on the concrete objective grounds that he may prove on the record the sample sent for analysis to the director could not be taken to be a representative sample of the article of food from which it was taken and if this contention is found to be correct, conviction based on the certificate will not be sustainable.
Reference on this aspect of the question may be made to the observations of the Division Bench of the Punjab High Court in Municipal Corporation of Delhi S. Nirajan Kumar and others "

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi S. Nirajan Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We would like to clarify that finality and conclusiveness has been attached only to the facts stated in the report of the Central Food Laboratory.

It is not, however, conclusive as to any other matter and it may still have to be ascertained whether adulteration as 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) disclosed in the report, of the Central Food Laboratory was due to certain factors for which an accused could not be held responsible.
In shoret the finality and conclusiveness are only to the extent that the sample as sent to the Central Food Laboratory contained what the report disclosed."

17A It is thus patent that according to the proviso to subsection(5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory is final and conclusive as to the state of the sample on the date on which the analysis was made.
Under sub section (3), this certificate supersedes the report of the Public Analyst given under sub section (1) of section 13 of the Act.

If prejudice is caused to the accused on account of the delay in the institution of the prosecution, as when the sample is rendered unfit for analysis in the meanwhile, or deterioration of the sample is proved to have occurred in the meanwhile, then the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt, as the prosecution itself, in such a case, prevents the accused from getting the final verdict to which he is entitled under section 13 of the Act.
In such a case, as held by the Supreme Court in Ghisa Ram's case (supra) the conviction cannot be upheld on the basis of 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) the reports of the Public Analyst.

But in case no prejudice is caused to the accused he cannot be allowed to escape the consequences under the law for such an anti social act which the legislature has ordained to be dealt with severely."

33 The Hon'ble High Court, in Bishan Sarup's case (supra), did not hold that since there was variance in the two reports exceeding .3% , therefore, the acquittal of the respondents was to be maintained.
Infact, the Hon'ble High Court, as mentioned in para 20 and 21 , had convicted the respondents (accused).
They were sentenced to pay fine.

I repeat that inspite of the fact that the two reports one of the Public Analyst and the other of Director CFL - were at variance exceeding .3%,
the respondents (accused) were not given any benefit.
They were convicted and sentenced to pay fine.

It suffers repetition that the contents found by the two experts were as under: Fat 6.7% (as per the report of the Public Analyst) Fat 7.2% (as per the report of the Director CFL) Non Fatty Solids 8.03% (as per the report of the Public Analyst) Non Fatty Solids 6.4% (as per the report of the Director CFL) 34

When the matter was considered by the Hon'ble 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court in Kashi Nath's case (supra), the Hon'ble High Court had on the basis of evidence of Director CFL, who was examined as a Court Witness, the variance of .3%, as had been deposed by the Court Witness, was taken into account.

entities.text: 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High court in Kashi Nath's case (supra) had taken into account the entire statement of the Director, CFL, to reach at the conclusion.

The Hon'ble High court did not lay down that the moment a variation of .3% in the two reports - i.e.,
Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
5

entities.text: Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.)

sentences.text: the one given by the Public Analyst and the other given by the Director CFL is found the accused has to be, with taking into account, other facts and evidence, straight away acquitted.

It was not held that the variation alone irrespective of the nature of evidence, nature of the food article, nature of violation noticed by the public analyst and the prescribed standard, would be decisive.

35 In the other judgements cited by ld. Counsel for the appellant the Hon'ble High Court had, in view of the judgement rendered by the Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath's case (supra), taken into account the variance between the reports of the Public Analyst and the Director CFL.
36 Use of an impermissible colour by itself, in view of rule 23 of PFA Rules, would make it a punishable offence.
Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) 37

In the present case, the opinion of the Public Analyst as per her report Ex. PW 1/H is as under:
" the sample does not confirm to the standards of mustard oil which also contains unpermitted synthetic colour.
Further there is violation of rule 32 (e) and (f)."
38 The Director, CFL, also found that it contained oil soluble coltar dye, therefore, opined that the sample of mustard oil was adulterated and contravened rule 32 (e) and (f) of PFA Rules.
39 In the present case no expert has been examined.

40 The question as to whether the court can take into account the minor deficiencies so as to term them in the nature of permissible error was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Municipal Committee Vs. Hazara Singh (1975) 1 SCC 794.

entities.text: Municipal Committee Vs. Hazara Singh (1975) 1 SCC 794
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that the standard fixed under the Act is one that is certain.
If it is varied to any extent, the certainty of a general standard would be replaced vagaries of a fluctuating standard.
Disadvantages all resulting under the predicting uncertainty and impossibility of arriving at fair and consistent decisions are great.
41 In that case a sample of milk was taken.
There was a minimal short fall in the percentage of milk solid not fat.
The plea of the 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) accused that there might have been a marginal error, while the analysis was conducted was rejected by the Magistrate.
In the appeal "the Ld. Sessions Judge ignored the minor deficiency which was in nature of permissible error".
He acquitted the accused.
Appeal preferred by the Municipal Committee was dismissed in limine by the Hon'ble High Court.
However the Municipal Committee approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
It was observed that the marginal error was rightly rejected by the Magistrate.
The observation of the Ld. Sessions Judge that "a minor error in the chemical analysis might have occurred" was opined by the Hon'ble Supreme Court to be not right.
42 The arguments that the SLP filed by the respondent in Kanshi Nath's judgement (supra) has been dismissed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 8/9/2011 is of no help.

I would like to add that the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dismissing the criminal appeal no. 1158/07 had also observed as under: "
However the question of law is kept open."
43 In this regard I would like to cite four judgements.
44 In State (DA) Vs. Satinder Kumar 2009 (1) JCC 258 decided on 14/11/2008 by our own Hon'ble High Court the acquittal of 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) the accused was set aside.
In that case the Public Analyst had found the extraneous material to the extent of 6% and the Director CFL had found the extent of extraneous material to the extent of 1.43%.

The Ld. MM had Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
6 highlighted the contradictions between the two reports and had held that the sample collected by the State was not a representative one.

entities.text: Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case the artificial colouring matter was also noticed.

The Hon'ble High Court, in para 6 of the judgement, observed that "the finding of the Ld. MM that the samples collected were not of representative one can't be sustained in as much as both the Public Analyst and the Director CFL have reached at a similar conclusion with regard to the presence of artificial colouring matter."
The order of the Ld. MM was set aside and the matter was remanded back for deciding it afresh.

45 In C. Mohd. Vs. State of Kerala 2007 (2) FAC 275 where in the sample of Moog Dal the Public Analyst had found .28% of Talc as foreign matter and Director CFL had found 1.363% Talc as Foreign Matter, the Hon'ble Supreme Court did not give any benefit of the variation.

entities.text: C. Mohd. Vs. State of Kerala 2007 (2) FAC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The conviction was upheld.
This case was decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on 18/11/2005.

46 In Subash Vs. State 2012 (1) JCC 431 the accused was 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA)
convicted under 7/16 PFA Act.
His appeal was dismissed by the Ld. ASJ.
His revision was also dismissed by our own Hon'ble High Court dated 21/11/2011.

Our own Hon'ble High Court in para 10 of the judgement observed as under:
" Keeping in view the scheme of the provisions of the Act which was intended to secure unadulterated food for the safety of the public, deviations in the prescribed standards of use of impermissible commodities in the eatables cannot be considered or termed as technical.
When the legislature intended to lay down specific standards of food items, the provisions need to be given its meaning in letter and spirit and nothing could be read in between them."

47 In Hari Pada Dass Vs. State of Bengal and Anr AIR 1999 SC 1482 the argument that minor variation was likely to take place on account of natural process and it was the duty of the prosecution to establish that there was no such chance of little variation, was not accepted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the ground that this contention has not been raised earlier and there was no sufficient evidence on the basis of which the finding to that effect can be made.

entities.text: Hari Pada Dass Vs. State of Bengal and Anr AIR 1999 SC 1482
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
48 Therefore, the arguments of ld. Counsel for the appellant that 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) in view of the variations in the two reports, benefit be given to the appellant, can't be accepted.
49
This brings me to the second limb of the arguments that Deepak Kalra had produced forged receipt Ex. PW 1/DA and the mustard oil in question had not been sold by the appellant to Deepak Kalra.
50 Trial court record reveals that Deepak Kalra had appeared as DW1 and had substantiated his defence.
In the cross examination, the witness had volunteered that this bill had been handed over to him by accused no.2 (the appellant herein ) himself.
He (witness) had never talked with accused no.2 (appellant) on telephone no. 241271 mentioned on the delivery challan Ex. PW 1/DA.
He had purchased the mustard oil from accused no.2 (the appellant herein) for the first time.
He does not know as to whether the phone no. 241271 mentioned on Ex. PW 1/DA was correct or not.
He denied the suggestion that accused no.2 (appellant herein) had never dealt with him (witness) or that he (appellant) used to issue bills in Hindi.

51 Now so far as the witnesses Gopal Prasad (DW2),
Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
7
Yogender Goel (DW3) and Rakesh Kumar (DW4) examined by the appellant are concerned, they are self supporting witnesses.
Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) 52

Sh Gopal Prasad (DW2) who claimed to have worked as a Munim in the firm of the appellant for the last 13 years has deposed that credit bill no.217 had been issued in the name of M/s. Goyal Traders, Ballabgarh, Haryana.
He has proved the carbon copies of the cash memos issued to other parties.
The same are Ex. DW 2/1 to 2/5.
He has also proved photocopy of the sales tax registration number.
The same is Ex. DW 2/6.
According to him the firm of the appellant had never manufactured or sold or supplied Jagat brand mustard oil to any one.
The mustard oil used to be sold under the trade name 'Chabi'.
53 In the cross examination conducted on behalf of Deepak Kalra, the witness admitted that the application for registration of 'Chabi' brand was made in 2002.
The telephone bills Ex. DW 2/7 to 2/10 are of 1999 to 2001.
The bills Ex. DW 2/1 to DW 2/5 are in respect of sales made at the shop.
He had not brough the bill book pertaining to the sale made outside the premises where from they carry their business in a routine way i.e shop situated at Ballabgarh, Haryana.
54 Yogender Goel (DW3) used to work as a supervisor in 1999 in the concern of the appellant.
He has deposed that the appellant was proprietor of M/s. Nikunj Industries.
The trade mark for the sale of 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) mustard oil of the firm was 'Chabi' and it was since the beginning of the firm.
55 Rakesh Kumar (DW4) has deposed that he used to work as an accountant in the firm of the appellant.
No sale of bill no. 427 had been made on 18/12/1999.
Ex. DA was not of their firm.
The witness produced copy of the Bahi Khata.
In the cross examination conducted on behalf of Deepak Kalra, the witness deposed that their firm was started in August1999.
56 Thus, the firm of the appellant had been started in August1999.
57 This particular admission of DW4 belies the statement of DW2.
58 The application for registration of 'Chabi' brand mustard oil was made in June2002.
The sample in question had been taken on 18/12/1999.
59 If the statements of DW2, DW3 and DW4 are taken into account, it shall be clear that the defence of the appellant is nothing but an after thought.
It can't be accepted.
60 The appellant did not appear as a witness to substantiate his defence.
Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) 61
The appellant could have examined the persons to whom he had sold the mustard oil vide the bills which are contained in the bill book produced by him.
In this bill book the carbon copies of the cash memos / bills dated 16/12/1999 have been exhibited as Ex. DW 2/1 to DW 2/5.
The last cash memo / bill in this book is dated 17/12/1999.
The cash memo Ex. PW 1/DA is dated 16/12/1999.
62 On Ex. PW 1/DA the phone number is mentioned as 241271.
On Ex. DW 2/1 to DW 2/5 the phone number of the office of the firm of the appellant is mentioned as 915241271.

It would thus show that the delivery challan from out of which Ex. PW 1/DA had been issued was got prepared prior to the preparation of the bill book which contains the Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
8

The code no. of that area is 0127.
A perusal of the book from out of which the originals of Ex. DW 2/1 to DW 2/5 are alleged to have been issued shows that it is a cash memo / bill book.
Ex. PW 1/DA shows that it is a delivery challan / credit memo.

63 Therefore, in view of the Full Bench judgement of our own Hon'ble High Court in Bishan Sarup's case (supra) and the views taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.Mohd. Vs. State of Kerala (supra) and by our own Hon'ble High Court in Subash's case (supra) and 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA) Satinder Kumar's case (supra), the argument of the appellant that in view of the variations, the appeal is liable to be accepted, is rejected.
64 The defence of the appellant is unacceptable.
65 Accordingly, so far as the conviction of the appellant is concerned, the same is maintained.
66 I would like to give a chance to the appellant to advance arguments on sentence.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kesar Devi Vs. Union of India 2003 VII AD (SC) 468 has held as under: " The judgment of a court is not to be interpreted like a statute where every word, as far as possible, has to be given a literal meaning and no word is to be ignored.
30 Since the question of right of the accused to have the second sample examined under section 13 (2) of the Act and the effect of the time lapse during the process was involved, therefore, Full Bench of the Hon'ble High Court had been constituted.
Once the Director of Central Food Laboratory has examined the 28/3/2012 Pawan Goel Vs The State (DA)
sample and has delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is the final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein.
The presumption attaching to the certificate again is only in regard to what is stated in it as to the contents of the sample Pawan Goyal S/O Sh Babu Ram vs The State ( D.A.) on 28 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155863573/
4 actually examined by the Director and nothing more.
Even after this certificate, it is open to the accused to show that in the facts of a given case and on the concrete objective grounds that he may prove on the record the sample sent for analysis to the director could not be taken to be a representative sample of the article of food from which it was taken and if this contention is found to be correct, conviction based on the certificate will not be sustainable.
Reference on this aspect of the question may be made to the observations of the Division Bench of the Punjab High Court in Municipal Corporation of Delhi S. Nirajan Kumar and others "
17A It is thus patent that according to the proviso to subsection(5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory is final and conclusive as to the state of the sample on the date on which the analysis was made.
Under sub section (3), this certificate supersedes the report of the Public Analyst given under sub section (1) of section 13 of the Act.
The Hon'ble High court did not lay down that the moment a variation of .3% in the two reports - i.e.,

the one given by the Public Analyst and the other given by the Director CFL is found the accused has to be, with taking into account, other facts and evidence, straight away acquitted.
It was not held that the variation alone irrespective of the nature of evidence, nature of the food article, nature of violation noticed by the public analyst and the prescribed standard, would be decisive.
